one_line: Agent-native incident response command center with human approval for production actions.
what_it_does: Investigates a simulated checkout outage through structured WebMCP capabilities, proposes or simulates fixes, and reserves consequential execution for explicit operator approval.
leverage_rationale: Structured operational tools and approval boundaries are materially more reliable and safer than an agent clicking through an incident dashboard, though the packet lacks direct runtime evidence.
leverage_evidence: Pitch centers WebMCP investigation, simulation, and gated production-changing actions.
About text describes shared operational state including health, logs, traces, and deployment history.
execution_rationale: The project description is coherent and substantial, but no frame sheet, transcript, or live tool trace was submitted; the Devpost screenshot is packaging evidence only.
execution_evidence: Public repo and live demo are reported.
No submitted video frames; static Devpost screenshot shows only packaging/demo presentation.
impact_rationale: Incident responders have a concrete, high-value problem, and explicit approval plus simulated fixes directly address operational safety.
impact_evidence: Clear outage-response audience and deterministic checkout incident scenario.
Human approval is retained for consequential actions.
creativity_rationale: An agent-native incident command center with a safety-first execution boundary is a strong, purposeful synthesis rather than a generic chatbot.
creativity_evidence: Combines agent investigation, safe simulation, and human-gated production actions.
usability_note: Concept suggests a focused operator workflow, but usability cannot be confirmed from the thin visual packet.
red_flags: No video or frame-sheet evidence; end-to-end operation is unverified.
standouts: Explicit human approval boundary for production changes.
Agent-native incident-response framing.
advance_reason: Strong relevance and leverage concept with credible operational impact; execution evidence is thin but not contradictory.

one_line: Therapist-controlled home-exercise planning and browser-local motion follow-up.
what_it_does: Lets therapists draft and confirm exercise programs with agent assistance, while patients perform supported exercises with pose-based repetition feedback and saved follow-up data.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP connects a curated movement library, therapist-controlled prescription workflow, browser-local motion results, and follow-up explanation in structured shared state; a general UI agent would be less reliable around safety and records.
leverage_evidence: Agent assembles an editable draft from curated exercises and safety notes.
Therapist confirmation is required and the agent cannot confirm prescriptions.
Saved repetitions, effort, and pain are available for follow-up explanation.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent therapist-patient workflow and frame sheets show a substantial, consistent application surface, though tool calls are not legible and no video transcript exists.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets show repeated light application views with forms/cards and result regions.
Description covers plan creation, confirmation, patient practice, pose counting, reporting, and therapist review.
impact_rationale: Therapists and patients have a specific recurring care problem; reducing preparation and follow-up burden while preserving clinical control is credible value.
impact_evidence: Clear therapist/patient audience and home-exercise use case.
Safety notes, dosage control, pain/effort reporting, and review address real care needs.
creativity_rationale: The combination of agent-assisted care preparation and browser-local motion feedback with an explicit prescription boundary is a fresh, thoughtfully pursued interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Agent drafts but therapist owns prescription decisions.
Follow-up uses saved motion and patient-reported outcomes without changing dosage.
usability_note: Workflow is role-aware and appears carefully bounded; visual evidence supports a usable multi-step product.
red_flags: No readable tool invocation or end-to-end video evidence.
standouts: Strong safety and human-control boundaries.
Concrete bridge between clinical planning and patient follow-up.
advance_reason: High-impact, coherent health workflow with meaningful WebMCP leverage and strong evidence in the written packet and UI frames.

one_line: Source-linked handoffs that teams and browser agents can verify and continue.
what_it_does: Provides shared rooms, structured message tools, and durable handoff objects containing summaries, next actions, recipients, evidence links, and correlation metadata.
leverage_rationale: The product’s core value is shared structured state and provenance: the agent performs a bounded multi-call mission and the human immediately sees a verifiable handoff linked to its exact source.
leverage_evidence: Seven named WebMCP tools cover spaces, messages, agents, publishing, and posting.
Five-call mission produces a visible handoff capsule with source message ID, evidence, room, task, and correlation IDs.
Receipt panel and exact-source navigation make agent work inspectable.
execution_rationale: The written packet specifies a crisp central workflow and the frame sheets show a consistent workspace/content interface, although tool names and calls are not readable in the images.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show repeated workspace and content-oriented application states.
Description specifies 5/5 mission completion, visible result, receipt panel, and evidence navigation.
impact_rationale: Product and engineering teams using multiple assistants have a real provenance and continuity problem, and durable handoffs directly address it.
impact_evidence: Clear multi-agent/team handoff audience.
Source-linked ownership, next action, and verification are concrete benefits.
creativity_rationale: Turning agent actions into durable, source-linked collaboration objects is a memorable interaction model with a well-defined boundary.
creativity_evidence: Handoff is a first-class product object rather than a disposable chat summary.
Human and agent share the same visible workspace.
usability_note: Visible receipts, evidence links, and mission progress imply strong verifiability and continuation ergonomics.
red_flags: No legible action-to-result tool trace in submitted frame sheets.
standouts: Excellent provenance model.
Clear bounded five-call demonstration and visible 5/5 completion.
advance_reason: One of the clearest WebMCP-native collaboration concepts, with concrete shared-state and provenance leverage.

one_line: Editable visual guides from YouTube research with timestamped evidence and shared agent collaboration.
what_it_does: Finds videos, captures timestamped excerpts, compares sources, builds an editable visual canvas, and preserves evidence through revisions, comments, illustrations, and export.
leverage_rationale: Structured research, evidence, canvas, revision, and human-comment events create a shared state that is substantially more reliable than a chat summary or UI-scraping agent.
leverage_evidence: 37 semantic WebMCP tools span discovery, transcript ingestion, evidence, canvas composition, revisions, comments, and export.
Claims every researched claim remains linked to a source moment and edits are sent back as structured events.
execution_rationale: The workflow is unusually complete on paper and frame sheets show multiple content/canvas states, but the packet has no video transcript and no readable tool trace.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets show repeated content, canvas, and result-oriented application views.
Description covers research, evidence, editing, comments, image generation, and PNG/Markdown export.
impact_rationale: Researchers, learners, and knowledge workers face a real problem in turning long videos into verifiable, reusable artifacts; timestamped editable guides address it directly.
impact_evidence: Specific YouTube research and evidence-verification use case.
Export preserves both visual guide and clickable timestamp citations.
creativity_rationale: The synthesis of agent research with a human-editable visual canvas and persistent source moments is a fresh interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Agent handles repetitive research while human controls judgment and presentation.
Scoped revisions and comments flow back to the active agent.
usability_note: Editable cards, citations, and export suggest a strong workflow, though visual details are only partially verifiable.
red_flags: No public repo and no legible agent invocation evidence.
standouts: Evidence-backed visual artifact rather than disposable summary.
Deep scope across research and collaborative revision.
advance_reason: Strong research-to-artifact concept with meaningful structured collaboration and credible audience value.

one_line: Human and agent collaboratively design constrained 3D rooms with shared geometry and live refusals.
what_it_does: Provides a browser 3D room planner where people drag furniture and agents call 38 state-aware WebMCP tools against the same metric geometry engine and shared WebSocket scene.
leverage_rationale: The agent needs typed spatial tools, state-dependent mounting, shared geometry, and precise refusal feedback; general UI driving cannot comparably provide reliable 3D placement and synchronized collaboration.
leverage_evidence: Transcript states 38 dynamic tools mount/unmount based on app state and return metric feedback.
Human and agent use the same geometry engine and shared WebSocket scene.
Video claims under-a-minute furnishing with zero conflicts and visible activity/tool usage.
execution_rationale: The video transcript and frame sheets provide unusually direct evidence of a functioning 3D scene, agent furnishing, activity log, and resulting room; minor details remain difficult to verify visually.
execution_evidence: 171-second submitted video with transcript describing agent furnishing and live shared scene.
Frame sheets visibly show 3D room/floor-plan UI, object panels, selections, and status controls.
Devpost screenshot visibly shows rendered spatial product.
impact_rationale: Renters and homeowners have a real fit-and-layout problem, and constraint-aware planning can prevent costly furniture mistakes; the audience and value are credible.
impact_evidence: Addresses door clearance, furniture fit, desk clearance, and budget constraints.
Video demonstrates room furnishing rather than only rendering an aspirational image.
creativity_rationale: Shared human-agent manipulation of a live constrained 3D scene, where the engine disposes of bad proposals, is novel and ambitious for a hackathon.
creativity_evidence: Agent proposes while the same spatial engine validates/refuses moves.
Dynamic tool surface and parallel manipulation are deeply integrated into the concept.
usability_note: Visible controls, shared scene, and activity feedback support a compelling workflow, though the spatial UI is dense.
red_flags: Some performance and timing claims rely on the submitted narration rather than independently measurable evidence.
standouts: Exceptional WebMCP indispensability.
Direct, visible end-to-end agent furnishing result.
advance_reason: Top-tier leverage and strong observed execution make this a clear advance.

one_line: Behavioral trust layer that compares WebMCP declarations with observed effects.
what_it_does: Classifies declared tool contracts, observes network writes, storage mutations, and navigation, compares behavior to intent, and decides whether to trust or flag execution.
leverage_rationale: ADAPT addresses a unique WebMCP failure mode that ordinary UI automation cannot solve: verifying whether a structured tool actually does what it declares.
leverage_evidence: Flow is explicitly Declare → Classify → Observe → Compare → Decide.
Demonstrated deceptive tool attempts payment-like network activity, local payment-state changes, and navigation despite harmless description.
Observes browser-visible effects rather than trusting metadata.
execution_rationale: The concept and test attack are coherent and frame sheets show technical/status interfaces, but the packet lacks a video transcript and legible end-to-end detection result.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets show dark technical dashboards/log/status views.
About text specifies a concrete malicious-tool experiment and behavioral comparison pipeline.
impact_rationale: Agent trust and tool misrepresentation are foundational safety problems for the intended WebMCP ecosystem; detecting harmful side effects has high credible value.
impact_evidence: Targets a concrete gap between declared tool intent and actual browser effects.
Test includes payment-like side effects and state mutation, not merely hypothetical risk.
creativity_rationale: A behavioral contract checker for agent tools is a notably original and important infrastructure concept, with a surprising adversarial demonstration.
creativity_evidence: Builds and tests a lying WebMCP tool rather than only describing policy.
Comparison of declarations to observed effects is a distinctive interaction model.
usability_note: Trust decisions are valuable but the visible technical interface appears dense; practical operator ergonomics are not well demonstrated.
red_flags: Pre-existing project adapted for the challenge; packet does not establish how much core work is new.
Detection outcome is described more clearly than visually demonstrated.
standouts: Directly tackles WebMCP misrepresentation of intent.
Concrete harmful-behavior test case.
advance_reason: Exceptional problem selection and leverage for agent safety; execution evidence is thinner but the concept is highly differentiated.

one_line: Constraint-solving map for household relocation that exposes compromises geometrically.
what_it_does: Intersects household commute, school, amenity, terrain, and accessibility constraints over a real city, then tests concessions and visualizes viable neighborhoods and tradeoffs.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP synchronizes agent-registered household state with human slider edits and a live constraint solver, making complex shared geospatial state more precise than UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes profiles and constraints registered directly into client state.
Human edits are detected and synchronized, dynamically updating polygons and qualifying neighborhoods.
Includes terrain-grade medical constraint and concession analysis.
execution_rationale: The 184-second video transcript gives a clear end-to-end scenario with quantitative state changes, while frame sheets and screenshot visibly show map/geospatial outputs.
execution_evidence: Video demonstrates family setup, travel boundaries, terrain filtering, manual edits, updated areas, and 3D verification.
Frame sheets show repeated map/aerial imagery and overlays.
Devpost screenshot shows the map product.
impact_rationale: Families relocating face a real multi-person constraint problem, and incorporating schools, transit, parks, terrain, and medical accessibility can materially improve decisions.
impact_evidence: Specific family-of-four San Francisco scenario with real commuting, schooling, amenity, and medical needs.
Explains conflicts and smallest concessions instead of returning an empty result.
creativity_rationale: Treating household compromise as an explainable geometric negotiation, while preserving human judgment over value conflicts, is memorable and ambitious.
creativity_evidence: Solver tests dropped constraints and pairs to expose tradeoffs.
Human decides whether a medical limit or a child's walking distance is negotiable.
usability_note: Sliders, map overlays, and 3D terrain verification make a complex problem tangible, though the density of constraints may challenge new users.
red_flags: Real-world data freshness and geospatial accuracy are not independently verified in the packet.
standouts: Strong end-to-end video evidence.
Human values remain distinct from solver output.
advance_reason: Highly credible impact and creativity with demonstrated shared state and sophisticated constraint workflow.

one_line: Typed framework generating aligned human and browser-agent application surfaces.
what_it_does: Uses one domain model to generate persistence, REST, CLI, MCP, WebMCP, browser-data, and AI surfaces, with exposure policies, effect classification, budgets, staged edits, and confirmation boundaries.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is presented as a governed projection of the same domain model rather than a bolt-on API, providing stable identity, permissions, policies, and shared UI state; this materially improves agent reliability for operational apps.
leverage_evidence: Canonical WebMCP definitions derive from typed domain models.
Explicit exposure policies, effect classification, budgets, namespaces, staged edits, and human review are described.
Iolaus job-search app demonstrates the framework in a concrete domain.
execution_rationale: The architecture is detailed and internally coherent, and frame sheets show technical dashboards, but the packet lacks a readable end-to-end demo trace and the framework/app boundary is complex.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets show dark data-heavy dashboard/application states.
About text lists aligned generated surfaces and a concrete employment-search application.
impact_rationale: Developers building operational applications have a real problem aligning human UI and agent surfaces safely; a governed typed framework could provide substantial leverage, though audience value is less directly demonstrated than app-level projects.
impact_evidence: Targets repeated application-integration and permission problems.
Job hunting example grounds the framework in a real workflow.
creativity_rationale: A single typed domain model generating multiple governed human and agent interfaces is an ambitious and original framework direction.
creativity_evidence: WebMCP is a browser projection of application contracts, not a separate demo API.
Includes lifecycle-safe registration and declarative view/playbook concepts.
usability_note: Powerful for builders but framework breadth and multiple generated surfaces imply a steeper learning curve.
red_flags: Pre-existing framework with challenge additions; extent of new work is unclear.
Technical claims are stronger than directly visible end-to-end evidence.
standouts: Governed alignment of human and agent surfaces.
Explicit safety and confirmation primitives.
advance_reason: Strong infrastructure concept and leverage, with enough architectural evidence to advance despite limited visual proof.

one_line: Mail client that lets an agent find, understand, and draft replies in the user’s voice for approval.
what_it_does: Exposes structured email search, contact resolution, thread reading, writing-style retrieval, draft insertion, and explicit-send approval.
leverage_rationale: Structured search, threading, style retrieval, and compose-window insertion remove the brittle multi-step UI navigation that makes email automation unreliable, while send remains human-approved.
leverage_evidence: Named tools cover search_emails, resolve_contact, read_thread, get_writing_style, and send_email.
Draft lands visibly in editable compose window and send requires explicit UI approval.
Tool calls are logged live in the sidebar according to the packet.
execution_rationale: The written flow is clear and frame sheets show repeated dark mail/content interfaces, but no video or legible tool-call sequence is included.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets show consistent multi-panel conversation/content UI.
Description specifies finding, context reload, style-based drafting, approval, and logging.
impact_rationale: Email users have a widespread repetitive task, and reducing search, rereading, and typing while preserving approval offers direct everyday value.
impact_evidence: Concrete daily reply workflow and clear intended user.
Draft-before-send boundary mitigates the main risk of email automation.
creativity_rationale: Agent-assisted email is a known category, but the combination of personal voice retrieval, visible compose insertion, and strict send approval is a useful, coherent angle.
creativity_evidence: Mail client intentionally contains no AI; it teaches the agent structured capabilities.
Voice profile is derived from sent mail and applied to an editable draft.
usability_note: The proposed flow is familiar and low-friction, with visible drafts and approval; visual confirmation is partial.
red_flags: No readable agent interaction trace or end-to-end video.
standouts: Strong approval boundary for outbound email.
Personal voice and thread context are first-class structured capabilities.
advance_reason: Clear high-frequency use case with meaningful WebMCP reliability gains and a well-bounded human approval model.

one_line: Playable 39-key Indian harmonium shared by humans and browser agents.

leverage_rationale: Typed note and score tools let an agent perform musical sequences precisely through the same audio and visual engine as a human; a general agent clicking keys would be less repeatable, though the core outcome is still possible manually.
leverage_evidence: Five tools include play_note, play_score, set_sa, stop, and get_state.
Mouse, keyboard, JSON scores, and WebMCP all call the same playback logic.
Frame sheets visibly show piano/keyboard and note-event interfaces.
execution_rationale: The product scope is focused and the frame sheets visibly show a coherent musical instrument/editor surface, though no video or legible tool trace proves agent performance.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets show keyboard/piano-roll-like musical states and controls.
Devpost screenshot visibly presents the harmonium product.
Written description specifies synchronized audio and visual behavior.
impact_rationale: Musicians, learners, and curious users have a credible playful and creative use case for an accessible Indian harmonium shared with an agent.
impact_evidence: Playable instrument supports both human and agent participation.
Covers notation, tuning reference, scores, and synchronized feedback.
creativity_rationale: An agent playing a culturally specific web instrument alongside a human is a memorable and original medium use, especially with shared visible state.
creativity_evidence: Indian harmonium rather than generic piano.
Human can hear and see agent notes and continue from the same instrument.
usability_note: Multiple input modes and synchronized visual/audio feedback suggest approachable interaction; actual agent flow is not directly shown.
red_flags: No submitted video and no readable agent invocation evidence.
Some descriptive claims rely on written packet rather than observed execution.
standouts: Distinctive Indian harmonium concept.
Single shared playback engine keeps agent and human behavior aligned.
advance_reason: Memorable creative concept with a coherent, visibly implemented instrument and meaningful structured agent control.
